subject: Recap: Redwood + Acme discovery — stakeholder map, procurement timeline, and exceptions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>, Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Redwood + Acme discovery — next steps & stakeholder map

Hi Sofia / Ben — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary:
- Use case: LLM-powered knowledge assistant for sales enablement and internal documentation search.
- Key decision criteria: latency (sub-200ms for retrieval), token cost/currency, data controls (VPC + audit logs), and formal SLA.
- Target go-live: proof-of-concept by end of Q3, production H2 2026.

Stakeholder mapping (from call):
- Economic buyer: Ben Thompson (VP of Product) — owns budget and final sign-off.
- Security / privacy: Sofia Ramos (Director, InfoSec) — will run the security review & questionnaire.
- Procurement / legal: procurement@acme.com (procurement team) — formal contract and SOW.
- Day-to-day champion: Javier Ortega (not on thread) — product manager driving integration.

Open items / asks for Acme:
1) Can you confirm the stakeholder list above and add any missing approvers?
2) Procurement timeline — you mentioned end of July for procurement review; please confirm dates and any blackout windows.
3) Security artifacts requested: SOC 2 report, data flow diagram, and our standard set of controls (we attached Acme_Security_Reqs.pdf noting the items you called out).

Internal note: attaching our Exception Form for potential SLA/discount requests. If you anticipate procurement requiring below-standard terms, please flag early so we can route approvals.

Attachments: Acme_Security_Reqs.pdf (requested by Acme during call), Redwood_MAL-Exception-Form.docx (exception form for SLA/discounts).

Next steps (agreed):
- Sofia: share full procurement timeline and initial questionnaire by Fri 7/16.
- Ben: confirm economic buyer and whether we should also invite Finance to the next call.
- Marissa (me): follow up with internal approvals if Acme requests exceptions.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short list of required security artifacts and the proposed mutual action plan.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood + Acme discovery — stakeholder map, procurement timeline, and exceptions

Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the attachments. Confirming the stakeholder mapping looks right from our side. A few notes from security/procurement: 

- Security: I will run the questionnaire and aim to get first-pass questions back by 7/16. We will need SOC 2 (type II) and the data flow diagram. Can you also include any recent pen-test summary?
- Procurement timeline: procurement team is targeting 7/30 for contract review, but that assumes standard commercial terms. If Redwood needs to provide an exception (discount greater than standard or SLA changes), that will push the timeline into August unless we can get internal approvals quickly.
- Exceptions: procurement has already asked whether we can get written approval for a pricing exception and an SLA commitment (they typically push for 99.99% uptime; we heard 99.9% was Redwood standard for this plan). They also asked about liability caps and data residency.

Attached: Acme_Security_Reqs.pdf (filled in by our team with clarifying notes).

If you can flag a potential exception now, we'll loop legal and procurement early to understand what documentation they need.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ramos | Director, Information Security, Acme Corp
sofia.ramos@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Acme procurement timeline + request for SLA/discount exception — approval request

Folks — forwarding Acme's note. They expect procurement review by 7/30 assuming standard terms. Two asks that will likely require internal approvals: 

1) Pricing exception: Customer has asked if we can consider an introductory discount for the first 12 months. They haven't given a target number yet; ballpark the rep thinks up to ~20% may be requested to align with budget.
2) SLA exception: procurement is asking whether we can commit to a 99.99% availability SLA and reduced latency SLO. Our typical commercial SLA for this offering is 99.9% with standard credit terms. Acme wants to know if we can provide stronger SLA and limited liability adjustments.

Why to approve (summary):
- Strategic pilot with Acme (large enterprise, multi-product rollout) — high ARR potential if POC succeeds.
- Short sales cycle if procurement timelines are honored.
- Competitive pressure: Acme is evaluating two other vendors who have indicated they can offer more aggressive commercial terms.

Risks / mitigations:
- Higher discount reduces initial ARR — request conditional approval for discount tied to expansion milestones and a 12-month term minimum.
- Tighter SLA increases operational exposure — propose a 60-day probation with enhanced observability and runbook commitments; limit SLA exception to specific services (read-only embeddings & retrieval) rather than entire platform initially.

Requested approvals (please reply by EOD 7/16):
- Pricing exception: approve up to 20% discount for first 12 months (yes/no + any cap).
- SLA: approve proceeding to negotiate 99.9% -> 99.99% request with the following guardrails: 60-day probation, scope-limited to specific routes, legal to sign off on liability cap language.

Attaching Redwood_MAL-Exception-Form.docx for signatures and to document approvals. If we can't get approvals by 7/16, procurement timeline slips and they'll likely move review to August.

Thanks — appreciate quick replies.
Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Acme procurement timeline + request for SLA/discount exception — approval request

Marissa / team — reviewed. Quick answers: 

- Pricing exception: provisional approval for up to 15% introductory discount for the first 12 months, contingent on: (a) signed 12-month term, (b) expansion clause tied to usage and an option to re-price after 12 months, and (c) Finance sign-off on margin impact.

- SLA exception: we can provisionally agree to negotiate toward 99.99% for specified endpoints, but final approval requires Legal to confirm liability/indemnity language. Approve a timeboxed experiment: 60-day probation with enhanced monitoring and an operational runbook. If SLA breaches occur during probation, revert to standard SLA and credit terms.

Action items: 
1) Rachel — please engage Legal to scope liability cap changes and draft a short addendum limited to the POC endpoints.
2) Monica — prepare a brief ops runbook and monitoring dashboard to be shared with Acme during the probation period.
3) Marissa — include the above guardrails in your commercial note back to Acme and request procurement to confirm acceptance of the conditional approval.

I want to keep momentum — if we can get procurement to accept the conditional terms, priority should be to lock the POC and instrument telemetry.

Vivek
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
